A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MF-LAL research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular-generation and ABFE simulation results for BRD4(2) and c-MET, baseline comparisons, ablations, and oracle-validation results.

after.justification: v2 retains original computational results and adds baseline evaluations, larger compound samples for selected comparisons, active-scaffold measurements, and decoder reconstruction results.

M1.justification: The hierarchical latent spaces, fidelity-specific decoders and SVGPs, uncertainty-based fidelity switching, and generation procedure remain. The revised loss expression does not establish an implementation change: v1 already documents KL-plus-reconstruction training and surrogate prediction from latent vectors.

E1.justification: Both retain molecular generation for BRD4(2) and c-MET using the same principal data sources. Appendix B.1 extends known-active/decoy oracle validation from BRD4(2) alone to c-MET, providing a limited expansion of validation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds MF-GP + ZINC250k, which selects queries from a fixed candidate pool, and DecompDiff. All previous comparators remain. DecompDiff was already cited in v1 but was not evaluated there; these are targeted additions to the existing comparison set.

E3.justification: Table 1 expands samples from 15 to 40 compounds for MF-LAL on both targets, Pocket2Mol on BRD4(2), and MF-AL-PPO on c-MET. Tables 1–2 introduce active-scaffold counts using target-specific ABFE thresholds and Tanimoto similarity below 0.4. Appendix C.2 adds exact SELFIES reconstruction evaluation. These substantially extend the evaluation design, while retaining the seven-day budget and molecular filters.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 and Figure 5 add decoder reconstruction trajectories across fidelities. Appendix B.1 extends validation of the oracle hierarchy to c-MET, and Table 2 adds active-scaffold outcomes to the existing ablations. The ablation variants and Figure 4's oracle-output trajectories are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports means and standard deviations without inferential tests. v2 adds Student's t-tests for overall and top-three ABFE means, binomial testing for active-scaffold proportions, and reported p-values. Appendix B.3 explains sample-size restrictions for scaffold comparisons. This substantially changes statistical reporting; the additional compounds do not establish repeated training runs or seed-based uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Results expand through two baseline rows, active-scaffold counts, and reconstruction trajectories. Table 1 replaces MF-LAL's c-MET mean of -6.5 with -7.1 kcal/mol while increasing the sample from 15 to 40, so this is not a controlled method improvement. The retained VAE + MF-GP c-MET second-best value changes from -7.7 to -6.0. Several Table 2 values also change. Appendix B.1 revises BRD4(2) docking/ensemble ROC-AUCs from 0.65/0.70 to 0.73/0.80 and adds c-MET results.

T1.justification: The relocated loss, v1 Equation 1 versus v2 Appendix A.2 Equation 2, changes the numerator from p(x|z) to p(x,z) and changes GP inputs and conditioning from x to the latent vector. These are mathematical revisions beyond renumbering. The acquisition, likelihood, and diversity expressions are otherwise retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction newly assert approximately 50% improvement in mean binding free energy. This quantifies the existing superiority claim; the central contributions of integrated surrogate/generative modeling and multi-fidelity query generation remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v1's limitations primarily concern oracle coverage and synthesizability. v2 adds substantive limitations concerning SVGP uncertainty away from inducing points, rejection of promising scaffolds by lower-fidelity screening, and variability under the fixed training budget. It also discusses hyperparameter sensitivity, explains reconstruction differences across fidelities, justifies emphasis on top compounds, and removes the qualification that fidelity 1 contributes very little.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies the fidelity-switch threshold as a hyperparameter, gives tuning advice concerning reconstruction/KL balance and diversity, and discloses a 32-compound oracle-validation dataset without establishing an increase from v1. Appendix B.2 specifies the new fixed-pool baseline's acquisition function and kernel and provides DecompDiff code-access information. Existing architecture, optimizer, hardware, and simulation details remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Bauer et al. (2016), Liu et al. (2017), Luo et al. (2021), Naguib et al. (2024), and Urbina et al. (2022), supporting limitations, evaluation choices, and the impact discussion. The related-work narrative and positioning against separate generative and surrogate models remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain. v2 adds local clarifications, moves mathematical details into Appendix A.2, subdivides Appendix C, and adds a statistical-tests subsection. It updates affiliation/publication text and replaces the acknowledgments section, including its funding and equity disclosure, with an impact statement.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column conference layout. Tables gain active-scaffold columns, and Table 1 also gains sample counts and significance markers. Figure 1 adds decoding annotations and an expanded caption; Figure 2 updates the c-MET lineup; Figure 5 is new. Figures 3 and 4 retain their content but are resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: The added fixed-candidate and DecompDiff comparisons, larger samples for leading methods, active-scaffold evaluation, and explicit statistical procedures strengthen the empirical argument. The expanded limitations also improve interpretation. These are useful but bounded gains: variability across complete training runs remains unquantified, and v1's funding/equity disclosure disappears. Overall, the evidence and explanations improve modestly, without resolving the principal uncertainty about run-to-run reliability.
